sec: Magnesium deficiency: causes, manifestations and treatment

items.q: Match the following deficiency settings — 1) Refeeding 2) Acute pancreatitis 3) Cetuximab … A) Redistribution B) Combined marked Ca/Mg depletion C) EGFR-related renal loss
items.exp: The page separates intracellular redistribution, pancreatitis-associated low Ca/Mg and drug-related renal loss. (Book p894)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the listed intracellular redistribution settings for low magnesium?
items.exp: The source lists DKA, hungry bone and refeeding under redistribution; FHH is linked to reduced renal magnesium excretion. DKA also involves total-body losses, so the label is simplified. (Book p894)

items.q: Match the following inherited magnesium defects — 1) Gitelman 2) Bartter type 1 3) Isolated TRPM6-related disease … A) Na–K–2Cl cotransporter B) Magnesium-channel defect C) Na–Cl cotransporter
items.exp: The chapter connects Gitelman with NCC, Bartter's NKCC2 form with the TAL, and isolated inherited magnesium deficiency with TRPM6. (Book p894)

items.q: A child has hypomagnesemia, nephrocalcinosis and a claudin-16/19 defect. Which urine-calcium pattern is physiologically consistent despite the source's 'hypocalciuria' wording?
opts: Normal calcium excretion in every case
items.exp: Claudin-16/19 disease is familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis. The source's hypocalciuria label conflicts with this mechanism and should be flagged. (Book p894)

items.q: The neuromuscular pathway linked to magnesium-deficiency seizures is increased ___-mediated excitability.
items.exp: The page associates magnesium deficiency with increased glutamate-mediated excitability and seizures. (Book p894)

items.q: A patient with low magnesium has an unusual ocular movement abnormality. Which finding is specifically listed?
items.exp: Vertical nystagmus appears in the neuromuscular feature list, alongside seizures. (Book p894)

items.q: Match the following hypomagnesemia systems — 1) Cardiac 2) Neuromuscular 3) Musculoskeletal … A) Seizures/nystagmus B) Reduced bone mass C) Tachyarrhythmia/long QT
items.exp: The symptoms tree connects magnesium deficiency to all three systems, not just a serum laboratory abnormality. (Book p894)

items.q: An ECG in a magnesium-depleted patient shows QT prolongation followed by polymorphic VT. Which rhythm is the key risk highlighted?
items.exp: The ECG illustration and branch list emphasize long QT, polymorphic VT and torsades. (Book p894)

items.q: Assess digitalis interactions: I Hypomagnesemia and hypokalemia increase susceptibility to digitalis toxicity. II The source's separate high-K/high-Mg digoxin note means every case of digoxin toxicity has those values.
items.exp: Low Mg/K are susceptibility factors. Acute severe digoxin poisoning can produce hyperkalemia, but the handwritten high-Mg note is not a universal diagnostic rule. (Book p894)

items.q: Which is not included in this page's associated-condition list for magnesium deficiency?
items.exp: The source lists MI, hypertension, severe low K/Ca, insulin resistance, migraine and colon cancer. Association does not prove magnesium replacement prevents each condition. (Book p894)

items.q: The magnesium intake figure printed for adults is approximately ___ per day.
items.exp: The page gives 420 mg or about 8.5 mEq/day; dietary requirements vary with age and sex. (Book p894)

items.q: The mild-deficiency entry lists three MgO tablets at 140 mg each. What stated daily total does that arithmetic give?
items.exp: Three times 140 mg is 420 mg. The source does not clearly distinguish tablet salt mass from elemental magnesium, so check the actual formulation before dosing. (Book p894)

items.q: Severe magnesium deficiency is accompanied by ventricular arrhythmia. Which replacement route does the page select?
items.exp: The severe/arrhythmia branch selects IV MgSO4; oral replacement belongs to mild disease. (Book p894)

items.q: Assess the MgSO4 entry: I The scan prints a 1–2 mg loading dose. II That milligram quantity is an appropriate standard adult dose for a life-threatening magnesium-responsive arrhythmia.
items.exp: The printed milligram loading dose is unsafe to learn as a clinical regimen. Emergency magnesium protocols use gram quantities; infusion timing depends on rhythm and hemodynamic context. (Book p894)

items.q: The source's continuation entry after initial IV magnesium is ___ over the next ___.
items.exp: The continuation line reads 4 g over 24 hours. This is a source reference, not a substitute for renal-adjusted monitored prescribing. (Book p894)

items.q: Assess replacement follow-up: I Serum normalization always proves full intracellular repletion. II The page advises continuing replacement after serum levels normalize.
items.exp: Serum normalization can precede restoration of tissue stores, which explains the continuation note; duration still requires clinical monitoring. (Book p894)

items.q: The potassium-sparing agents mentioned as possible adjuncts for magnesium wasting are ___ and ___.
items.exp: The source names amiloride and triamterene; loop and thiazide agents can instead aggravate magnesium losses. (Book p894)
